rv.q: Rough-and-ready verbatim account of the Kenmure Street protest
Leaving the Citz, one carries the lingering echo of a community's defiant chant – a timely reminder that when the vans arrive on our streets, our greatest defence is each other.
As with many works of formally ambitious theatre, however, where there are some genuinely successful moments, there are also some which miss their target.

Whilst there is much promise, excitement and intentional storytelling to appreciate in this staging of inspiring modern local history through dance-theatre, it fails to reach the heartening heights of the deft, exemplary recreation it aspires to achieve and, at points, demonstrates it can deliver.

cn.t: Critics give this dance-theatre piece about Glasgow's 2021 immigration raid standoff a middling reception, awarding it three stars. The work captures a poignant community moment but doesn't fully deliver on its powerful real-life subject matter.
